pr_title: backupccl: make backup and restore more defensive to stats collections failures
pr_body:
Release justification: low risk, high benefit change to existing functionality.

Release note: None

Fixes: #61199
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/61420)
Stats collection in restore also happens during job execution as a result of which we cannot send back a notice to the user.

> Stats collection in restore also happens during job execution as a result of which we cannot send back a notice to the user.

I think that we can check if stats _exist_ in the backup during planning time (we don't today, but we can add that check). If there are no stats included in the backup at all, that means that we won't restore any.

The notice still looks wonky even though I'm using the method just like other places are. I suspect it's something to do with planHooks, I'm still looking into it. I also made restores not fail when they are unable to open the stats file for any reason, and added a test to verify this.

Filed a CLI issue - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/61516. It seems like the issue is on the client-side where we flush notices at the wrong time. I'll split the notice part of this PR out to another one, which can be checked in after the issue is resolved.
@dt just putting this on your radar for a stamp 🙂

flake on unrelated test.

bors r+

issue_context.title: backupccl: make BACKUPs more defensive on stats collection failures
issue_context.body: We should not be failing the BACKUP if we run into an error computing table stats right at the end of job execution. More likely than not, the customer would like their data to be backed up, and are okay with an expensive stats recomputation on RESTORE. We should log a warning instead.
comments:
Agree that the default behavior should be to continue on failure of ‘optional’ data like stats -- with logging of course.

Is there such thing as ‘partial’ stats? If a particular stat fails, can we restore other stats?

review_comments: Since the stats were made to be more resilient, would this test pass before this change anyway?
Yeah it would, i went back and forth on the relevance of the test after that fix. I'm onboard with deleting it if you feel like it's not lending us any protection from a regression.
I think it's fine to keep this as a regression test to ensure that both backup and stats remain defensive about this particular issue. Just wanted to verify I was understanding what was under test.
